commitResults.messageBody:
The UI has no automated tests, so console behavior can change
unnoticed. The "list" command also omits the "Here are the tasks in
your list:" header that the project specification shows before the
numbered tasks.

Let's add a repeatable end-to-end UI test setup and fix the header:
- Add test/ui-test-plan.md with nine test cases, each stating its
  aim, input and expected output, and test/run-ui-tests.py to run
  them and stop at the first failure.
- Add the test-ui skill so the plan is run the same way each time
  and the console session is shown.
- Print the header in "list" so the output matches the spec.
- Require in AGENTS.md that every code update refreshes the plan
  (if needed) and runs the test-ui skill.

Keeping the plan as a markdown file lets test cases be reviewed and
extended without touching the runner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Replace magic numbers with constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Command parsing uses bare numbers such as substring(5), substring(7)
and indexOf(...) + 6. Each number is the length of a command word or
a marker like "/by ", but a reader has to count characters to see
that, and changing a keyword would silently break the parsing.

Let's name the command words and markers as constants and derive each
offset from the constant's length:
- Add PREFIX_MARK, PREFIX_UNMARK, COMMAND_TODO, COMMAND_DEADLINE,
  COMMAND_EVENT, MARKER_BY, MARKER_FROM and MARKER_TO.
- Use constant.length() instead of hard-coded offsets.
- Drop the "input.length() > n ? ... : """ guards in the parse
  methods. They are only reached when the input equals the command
  word or starts with it, so substring(length) is always safe.

This follows the code quality guideline on avoiding magic numbers:
the intent is now visible in the code and the keyword and its offset
can no longer drift apart. Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases
pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Extract isCommand helper
commitResults.messageBody:
The command dispatch repeats the same two-part condition for todo,
deadline and event: input.equals(word) || input.startsWith(word + " ").
Each repetition is a long expression a reader has to parse, and a
mistake fixed in one copy could be missed in the others.

Let's move the check into an isCommand(input, command) method and call
it from the dispatch chain.

This follows the code quality guidelines on avoiding complicated
expressions and duplication (DRY): the dispatch now reads as a list of
command names and the matching rule lives in one place. Behavior is
unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Extract duplicated usage messages
commitResults.messageBody:
parseDeadline and parseEvent each print the same usage error in two
places, once when a marker is missing and once when a part is empty.
The copies were made by copy-paste, so changing the wording means
finding and editing every copy, and they can drift apart.

Let's define MESSAGE_DEADLINE_USAGE and MESSAGE_EVENT_USAGE constants
and print those from both checks.

This follows the code quality guideline on minimizing duplication
(DRY): each message is written once and reused. The text is
identical, so behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Extract readInput helper
commitResults.messageBody:
main reads input in two places with the same expression that falls
back to "bye" at end of input, and a comment in one of them explains
why. Readers must notice the two copies are identical, and the reason
for the fallback is hidden inside the loop.

Let's move the expression into a readInput(Scanner) method whose
Javadoc states the fallback and why it exists.

This follows the code quality guidelines on minimizing duplication
(DRY) and commenting WHAT and WHY: the rule is written once, with its
rationale in the method header, and main reads at a higher level of
abstraction. Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Stop reusing taskCount parameter in addTask
commitResults.messageBody:
addTask receives the current task count and then increments that same
parameter to produce the new count. The name taskCount first means the
old count and later the new one, and a reader has to track where the
meaning changes.

Let's keep taskCount unchanged and store the result in a new local
variable, newTaskCount, which is printed and returned.

This follows the code quality guideline on not recycling variables or
parameters: each variable has one purpose for its whole lifetime.
Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Extract handleCommand from main
commitResults.messageBody:
main starts the program, reads input and, inside its loop, also picks
the right action for each command with a six-way if-else chain. The
method is over 30 lines and mixes high-level steps (banner, read,
exit) with command-level detail.

Let's move the dispatch chain into handleCommand, which runs one
command and returns the updated task count. main keeps only the
startup, read loop and shutdown.

This follows the code quality guidelines on avoiding long methods and
the Single Level of Abstraction Principle: main now reads as the
program's outline, and the command dispatch can be read and changed
on its own. Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Rename misleading variables and parameters
commitResults.messageBody:
In the parse methods a local variable named "args" holds the text
after the command word, but "args" normally means the command-line
arguments of main, which is also in this class. The boolean
parameters named "done" in markTaskByInput and setTaskDone do not
say they are flags, unlike the isDone field in Task.

Let's rename the locals to "arguments" and the boolean parameters to
"isDone".

This follows the code quality guidelines on avoiding misleading names
and on naming related things alike: "arguments" no longer looks like
main's args, and boolean names match the isXxx style used elsewhere.
Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add specific error messages for invalid input
commitResults.messageBody:
Bad input gets vague or misleading replies. A malformed deadline or
event always shows one generic message, "mark" without a number is
reported as an unknown command, "mark abc" and "mark 9" give little
help, a trailing "/by" is reported as a missing "/by", and stray
spaces around a command make it unrecognised. The user cannot tell
what is wrong or how to fix it.

Let's make every error say what went wrong and how to correct it,
and keep the chatbot running so the user can simply retry:
- Add a printError(problem, fix) helper so all errors share one
  format and end with the horizontal line.
- Report each deadline and event problem separately: missing
  marker, empty description, empty time, and /to before /from.
- Report a missing, invalid or out-of-range task number, and
  marking when the list is empty, each with its own message and
  the valid range.
- Name the unknown command and list the available commands, and
  report blank lines.
- Trim input so spaces around a command are ignored, and match
  /by, /from and /to as whole words so "/tomorrow" is not read
  as "/to".
- Extend test/ui-test-plan.md from 9 to 15 test cases to cover
  each error and to check the chatbot keeps running after errors.

Explaining the fix together with the problem lets the user correct
the command without reading the documentation. The 100-task limit is
intentionally left as is, as the project allows an array of 100.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize task classes into eric.task package
commitResults.messageBody:
Todo, Deadline, Event and Task sit in the same package as Eric, the
program entry point, so the package says nothing about how the
classes relate. As more classes are added, unrelated classes would
pile up in one package.

Let's group the classes that model tasks in their own package:
- Move Task, Todo, Deadline and Event to eric/task, declared as
  package eric.task.
- Import the four classes explicitly in Eric, as the coding
  standard forbids wildcard imports.

A separate eric.task package keeps the entry point apart from the
task model, and new task types have an obvious place to go. Eric
stays in package eric, so the main class name and the run
instructions are unchanged. Behavior is unchanged; all UI test cases
pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Packages into master
commitResults.messageBody:
The task classes now live in their own eric.task package, apart
from the Eric entry point, so the package structure reflects how
the classes relate.

Let's merge the branch with a merge commit, rather than a
fast-forward, so the history shows this work as one unit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command and store tasks in a List
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot remove a task once it is added, and tasks are kept in
a fixed-size Task[] array with a separate taskCount that every
method has to pass around and keep in sync. The array also limits
the list to 100 tasks.

Let's add a "delete INDEX" command and move the tasks into a
List<Task> backed by an ArrayList:
- Add deleteTaskByInput, which removes the task and prints the
  removed task and the new task count.
- Share the task-number checks between mark, unmark and delete in
  findTaskIndex, so all three accept the same numbers and report
  the same errors, naming their own command.
- Replace the array and taskCount with List<Task>. The list's size
  is the task count, so the count can no longer get out of sync,
  and MAX_TASKS and its limit are removed.
- Add delete to the list of available commands in error messages.
- Extend test/ui-test-plan.md from 50 to 62 test cases covering
  delete, its errors, and delete mixed with other commands, and
  document delete in docs/README.md.

A List supports removal directly and shifts later tasks down, which
is what the renumbering after a delete needs. ArrayList is the
simplest List that fits. Behavior of the existing commands is
unchanged; all UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Save tasks to data/duke.txt after each change
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks exist only in memory, so everything the user adds is lost when
Eric exits. The project requires the task list to be saved to the
hard disk automatically whenever it changes. Loading it back at
startup is planned as a later step.

Let's write the saved file, which is the first half of that feature:
- Add a Storage class in a new eric.storage package. It writes one
  line per task to data/duke.txt, using Path.of so the path is
  relative and works on any operating system, and creates the data
  folder and the file if they do not exist yet.
- Add toFileString to Task, Deadline and Event so each task writes
  its own line, e.g. "D | 0 | return book | June 6th". Events use
  separate start and end columns, because the start and end are
  stored separately and this keeps them readable later.
- Save after every add, mark and unmark in Eric. If saving fails,
  print an error message instead of crashing.
- Ignore the /data/ folder in .gitignore, as it holds user data.
- Run each UI test case in its own empty temporary folder, so the
  tests never overwrite real saved data and always start with no
  data file. Test cases may now check the saved file, and the test
  plan grows from 50 to 58 cases covering the new behavior.

Loading the file is left out on purpose, so this commit stays small
and the file format can be settled before it is read back. All UI
test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add present-changes-visually skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Reviewing a change means reading raw git diff output in the
terminal, which is hard to follow across many files. The project
needs a way to present changes visually, for example to review a
feature before committing it.

Let's add a project skill that generates one self-contained HTML
page showing each changed file as a side-by-side before/after diff.
It is based on the se-edu skill-present-changes-visually repository
(commit 95c044c), adapted for Claude Code:
- Use .claude/skills paths instead of .codex/skills.
- Point the commit message guidance to the seedu-git-standard skill.
- Leave out the Codex-only agents/openai.yaml file.

The bundled generator uses only the Python standard library and only
runs read-only git commands, so there is nothing extra to install.
Output goes to the git-ignored _temp folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Task class: Add fromFileString to parse a line
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks can be written to the save file with toFileString, but
nothing can turn a saved line such as "D | 0 | return book | June 6th"
back into a task, so the file cannot be loaded at startup.

Let's add the reading half next to the writing half, so the file
format is defined in one class:
- Add Task.fromFileString, which checks the line and creates the
  Todo, Deadline or Event it describes. An invalid line throws an
  IllegalArgumentException whose message says what is wrong, e.g.
  "expected 4 columns for a D task but found 3".
- Move each type letter into a TYPE_ICON constant in Todo, Deadline
  and Event, so getTypeIcon and the reader share one definition
  instead of repeating "T", "D" and "E".
- Name the flag values and column positions as constants instead of
  using bare numbers.

The reader lives in Task, next to toFileString, so a change to the
format only has to be made in one place. Nothing calls the new
method yet, so behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage class: Add load to read the save file
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage can write the task list to data/duke.txt but cannot read it
back, so saved tasks are lost on the next start. A missing file must
not be an error, because it will not exist the first time Eric runs
on a new computer.

Let's add Storage.load:
- Return an empty list if the file does not exist, rather than
  failing.
- Ignore blank lines.
- Skip lines that are not in the save file format and report each
  with its line number and reason, so one bad line does not make the
  rest of the file unreadable.
- Return the tasks and the warnings together in a small LoadResult
  record, so the caller can decide how to show the warnings.

Skipping bad lines, instead of stopping at the first one, keeps
every task that can still be read. Nothing calls load yet, so
behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Load saved tasks when Eric starts
commitResults.messageBody:
Eric saves the tasks after every change but always starts with an
empty list, so the saved data is never used and the next save
overwrites it.

Let's load the saved tasks before the first command is read:
- Add loadTasks, which fills the task array from Storage.load.
- Show any skipped lines to the user, and say they will be dropped
  the next time the tasks are saved.
- If the file cannot be read at all, say so and start with an empty
  list, so Eric never fails to start.
- If the file has more tasks than the array can hold, load the first
  100 and warn, instead of crashing with an index error.

Reporting these problems at startup keeps the user informed without
stopping them from using Eric. When there is no file, or it is fine,
nothing extra is printed, so the usual startup output is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Test runner: Let tests start with a saved file
commitResults.messageBody:
Every UI test case starts with no data file, so loading cannot be
tested: a test has no way to give Eric a file to load. The check of
the saved file also compares trailing spaces in the actual file but
not in the expected one, which fails on a file that has a space-only
line.

Let's allow a test case to start from a given file:
- Add an optional "Initial file (data/duke.txt)" block to the test
  plan format. The runner writes it to the test's temporary folder
  before Eric starts, and shows it in the session record.
- Ignore trailing spaces in the actual saved file too, as the test
  plan already says for all comparisons.
- Document the new block in the test-ui skill.

Test cases without the block behave as before, so the existing test
cases need no changes and all of them still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Test plan: Add UI test cases for loading tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving has UI test cases, but the new loading code has none, so it
could break without anyone noticing.

Let's add eight test cases (TC59 to TC66), each starting from a
given save file:
- Load every task type and done flag, and leave the file unchanged.
- Change and extend loaded tasks, and check the file is rewritten.
- Load an empty file, and a file with blank lines.
- Skip six kinds of malformed line, each reported with its line
  number and reason, and drop them on the next save.
- Load UTF-8 text, inner spaces and symbols unchanged.
- Check task numbers against the loaded tasks.
- Load a file of 101 tasks without crashing, keeping the first 100.

The malformed-line case covers each error message in one test, so a
change to any of them is caught. All 66 test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: User guide: Document saving and loading
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not say that Eric keeps the tasks between runs,
where they are stored, or what the file looks like.

Let's add a "Saving and loading" section that states:
- Tasks are saved to data/duke.txt each time the list changes, and
  loaded when Eric starts.
- The folder and file are created automatically, so a first run
  needs no setup.
- The format of each task line and the meaning of the done flag.
- Lines that cannot be read are skipped and reported.

Users can then find and read the file, and know what to expect on
the first run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Reject a save file that is not valid
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading skips the lines it cannot read and keeps the rest. That
hides a damaged file: Eric starts with part of the tasks, says so
only in a warning, and the next save silently drops the skipped
lines. A file with more tasks than the array holds is cut off the
same way.

Let's treat an unusable save file as a whole and reject it:
- Add StorageException, carrying a reason in plain words.
- Make Storage.load throw it if the file is a folder, cannot be
  read, is not valid UTF-8 text, or has any invalid line. The message
  lists every invalid line with its line number and reason. A missing
  file or folder still gives an empty list, as on a first run.
- Replace the LoadResult record, which is no longer needed, with a
  plain list of tasks.
- In Eric, report the reason, start with an empty list, and tell the
  user the file will be replaced by the next change and how to keep
  it: close Eric and fix or move the file. Also reject a file of more
  than 100 tasks, instead of loading only the first 100.
- Update the two test cases that expected skipped lines.

Rejecting the whole file means Eric never runs on half of the user's
data without saying so, and every problem in the file is shown at
once so it can be fixed in one go. All UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Test runner: Support unusual starting files
commitResults.messageBody:
A test case can give Eric a starting save file, but only as plain
lines of text. Several situations that loading must survive cannot
be written that way: the data folder existing without the file, a
folder where the file should be, a file that is not valid text, and
a file saved with Windows line endings. The runner also crashes
while looking at the saved file if that path is a folder.

Let's let an "Initial file" block describe those situations with
one special line:
- "(data folder only)", "(folder)" and "(invalid utf-8)" create the
  situation they name.
- "(windows line endings)" as the first line writes the remaining
  lines ending with CRLF.
- Only read the saved file if it is a file, so a folder in its place
  no longer crashes the runner.
- Document the special lines in the test-ui skill.

Special lines are used instead of separate fields so that the plan
keeps its one simple shape, and ordinary test cases stay unchanged.
All existing test cases still pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Test plan: Add edge cases for loading a save file
commitResults.messageBody:
The loading code now handles missing and unusable files, but the
test plan only covers the usual cases, so a change to these edge
cases could go unnoticed.

Let's add eight test cases (TC67 to TC74), each starting from the
situation it names:
- The data folder exists without the file: empty list, and the file
  is created on the first change.
- A folder where the file should be, and a file that is not valid
  text: each is rejected with its own reason and Eric keeps running.
- A file saved with Windows line endings loads correctly.
- A file with only blank lines gives an empty list without warning.
- Six more kinds of invalid line: a lower-case type, a leading
  space, a done flag that is not 0 or 1, too many columns, and an
  empty time.
- A | without spaces around it is ordinary text.
- A rejected file is left unchanged until the list changes.

The missing-folder and missing-file cases are already covered by the
earlier tests, which start without a data folder. All 74 UI test
cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Eric class: Reject text that breaks the save file
commitResults.messageBody:
The save file separates columns with " | ". A task typed as
"todo a | b" is saved as "T | 0 | a | b", which has one column too
many. The next start would reject the whole file, so one ordinary
command could make Eric unable to load its own saved tasks.

Let's refuse such text when the command is typed:
- Make Task.FILE_SEPARATOR public so Eric can check against the same
  separator that the file format uses.
- Add hasNoFileSeparator, which prints an error naming the separator
  and suggesting a fix, and use it for the description of a todo, and
  for the description and dates of deadlines and events.

A | without spaces around it, such as "a|b", does not contain the
separator, so it is still allowed. Rejecting the text at input is
simpler than escaping it in the file, and it keeps the file format
easy to read and write by hand. All UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Test plan: Add cases for text that breaks the file
commitResults.messageBody:
Eric now refuses task text containing " | ", but no test checks
that, or that a | without spaces around it still works and can be
read back.

Let's add four test cases (TC75 to TC78):
- Reject a spaced | in a todo description, and in each text part of
  a deadline and an event, and save nothing.
- Accept a | at the start, middle and end of the text, and check the
  lines written to the file.
- Load a saved line whose text ends with a |.
- Mix rejected commands between valid ones, and check that neither
  the list nor the saved file is disturbed.

Together with the loading tests, this covers the file format in both
directions. All 78 UI test cases pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: User guide: Explain invalid save file handling
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide's saving section still says that unreadable lines
are skipped, which is no longer true, and it does not mention the
text Eric refuses to save.

Let's update the section:
- Say that a file that cannot be used is rejected as a whole, what
  Eric reports, and that the file is replaced on the next change, so
  it must be fixed or moved first to keep it.
- Say that task text cannot contain a | with spaces around it.

Users can then fix a damaged file without losing their tasks, and
know why a command with " | " in it is refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: implemented level-6 delete feature
implemented level-7 saving and loading
Add Gradle build with shadowJar for a fat JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
Eric can only be run from an IDE or by compiling the sources by
hand, so it cannot be handed to someone else as a single file.

Let's add a Gradle build that can package Eric as one runnable JAR:
- Add build.gradle with the java, application and shadow plugins.
  The application plugin names eric.Eric as the main class, and
  shadowJar writes the fat JAR to build/libs/eric.jar.
- Add the Gradle wrapper (gradlew, gradlew.bat and gradle/wrapper),
  taken from the template's gradle branch, so that nobody needs to
  install Gradle and everyone builds with the same version (9.6.1,
  which supports Java 25).
- Add settings.gradle to fix the project name as "eric", instead of
  using the name of the folder.
- Turn off the plain JAR, which is not needed, and rename its output
  so it cannot clash with the shadowJar output.
- Leave out the template's JUnit dependencies, because the project
  has no JUnit tests.

The shadow plugin was chosen because it bundles everything into one
file that runs with "java -jar". The build output is already ignored
by .gitignore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: README: Explain how to build and run the JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The README explains how to set up the project in an IDE, but not how
to build Eric as a JAR file, where the file is created, or how to
run it.

Let's add a "Building and running a JAR file" section that states:
- The command to build it (./gradlew shadowJar, or gradlew.bat
  shadowJar on Windows) and that the first build needs internet.
- The JAR is created at build/libs/eric.jar.
- It is run with "java -jar build/libs/eric.jar", and saves its
  tasks in a data folder next to where the command is run.
- ./gradlew run runs Eric without building the JAR.

Readers can then build and run the JAR without reading build.gradle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: implemented A-Jar
